content.user_title: Manage Cooper Email Bounces and Suppressions
content.value_statement: Bounces and spam complaints can interrupt delivery and harm sender reputation. This skill guides Cooper Email investigations, rate checks, and consent-based suppression management.
actual_capabilities: Guide suppression lookups to identify affected addresses, reasons, source message identifiers, and timestamps.
Connect suppression records to source messages and bounce or complaint events through documented Cooper tools.
Request delivery counts, bounce rates, and complaint rates using Cooper metrics.
Apply distinct response guidance for failed addresses, spam complaints, and rising delivery failure rates.
Guide suppression removal only after user confirmation of address validity and recipient consent.
Distinguish suppressions from block and allow lists, with references to the relevant list management tools.
limitations: Requires a connected Cooper Email integration; this skill provides instructions, not tool implementations.
Suppression listing requires an account-level key or OAuth; an inbox-scoped key receives permission_denied.
Cannot guarantee delivery or independently verify address validity and recipient consent.
References separate webhook and owner approval skills; it does not implement those workflows.

use_cases.title: Resolve a suppressed recipient
use_cases.description: Find why a customer address was suppressed and report the source message before requesting a correction or consent confirmation.

use_cases.title: Investigate delivery trends
use_cases.description: Review bounce and complaint rates, inspect related events, and recommend slower sending or stricter outbound controls.

use_cases.title: Handle application delivery errors
use_cases.description: Distinguish recipient_suppressed from recipient_blocked and identify the appropriate suppression or list management workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a suppression
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain recipient_suppressed in Cooper Email and identify what information I need to investigate it. Do not change account settings.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a recipient
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate why [recipient] is suppressed in Cooper Email. Summarize the reason, source message, and related events without removing the suppression.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect a specific delivery failure.

prompt_templates.title: Review delivery rates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Cooper Email bounce and complaint rates for the default reporting period. Summarize related events and recommend actions without changing outbound policies.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a controlled restoration
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate suppression and block-list status for [recipient]. Ask for confirmation of validity and consent before suppression removal; keep list policies unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate checks before a state-changing operation.

output_examples.input: Cooper reports recipient_suppressed. The suppression record shows a bounce. What should I do?
output: The address is suppressed because of a bounce.
Do not retry the same address. Ask for a corrected address.
Remove the suppression only after confirming the address is valid and the recipient wants the mail.

output_examples.input: My inbox-scoped key returns permission_denied when listing Cooper suppressions.
output: Suppression listing requires an account-level key or OAuth.
Use an authorized account connection before investigating the suppression record.
Do not paste credentials into the conversation.

output_examples.input: Cooper reports recipient_blocked. Is this the same as recipient_suppressed?
output: No. A block or allow list match can return recipient_blocked.
Suppressions are separate and can result from bounces, complaints, or manual action.
Inspect list entries before considering policy changes. Removing a suppression does not resolve a list restriction.

best_practices: Inspect the suppression reason, source message, and related events before recommending action.
Confirm address validity and recipient consent before removing a suppression.
Monitor bounce and complaint rates, slow sending when rates rise, and review recipient lists.
anti_patterns: Retrying the same bounced address without correcting the underlying problem.
Removing suppressions merely to bypass spam complaints or recipient consent.
Treating suppressions and block or allow lists as the same control.

faq.question: What does recipient_suppressed mean?
faq.answer: Cooper has suppressed the address and rejects the send with HTTP 403. The rejected message is not sent, stored, or counted against the plan.

faq.question: Which credentials can list suppressions?
faq.answer: Use an account-level key or OAuth. An inbox-scoped key receives permission_denied.

faq.question: When can I remove a suppression?
faq.answer: Only after the user confirms that the address is valid and the recipient wants the mail.

faq.question: How should I handle a spam complaint?
faq.answer: Stop mailing the recipient and notify the user. Do not remove the suppression simply to resume sending.

faq.question: How can I check bounce and complaint rates?
faq.answer: Use cooper_get_metrics with kind set to rates. The documented default period is the last 30 days.

faq.question: Does this skill install Cooper tools or configure webhooks?
faq.answer: No. It guides existing Cooper tools and references a separate webhook skill. A working Cooper integration is required.
